transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brought me in is... I just don't feel like myself anymore. I barely talk to people lately. I just go sort of flat and quiet. I work as a janitor, and honestly, even just getting started on my cleaning route feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. It's just taking everything out of me to get going.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people around you don't seem to notice?

Yeah, actually, I do. Um... when I’m mopping after hours, I’ll hear a man’s voice. He'll say my name, or... or tell me I’ve missed a spot. It sounds as clear as if he’s standing right by the stairwell. But whenever I look over to check, there’s nobody there.
Are you only hearing this voice when you are feeling deeply depressed, or do you hear it even during times when your mood is relatively stable?

No, it's... it's not just when I'm really down. There was a stretch of several weeks recently where my mood had actually lifted some. I was getting through my meals and my work a little better, you know? But... I still heard my name in the stairwell. And I stayed convinced that the hallway cameras were being used to track me. So, yeah, it happens even when I'm feeling relatively stable.

During the times when you are having these experiences with the voice or the cameras, have you ever felt like you were experiencing a distinct period of a very low or very high mood that lasted for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I have. When I was at my absolute lowest... you know, barely eating, feeling guilty about everything, and honestly just thinking I might not want to wake up... that definitely lasted for a few weeks. And during that whole time, I was also hearing that man's voice at work, and I still believed people in the building were watching me. So, yeah, those things were definitely happening at the same time during that really low period.
Have you ever experienced these voices or the belief about the cameras for a period of at least two weeks when you were not feeling significantly depressed or having any other major mood changes?

Yeah, like I was saying just a minute ago, that's exactly what happened. There was that stretch of a few weeks recently where my mood was actually okay. I wasn't feeling depressed, and I was getting through my work and eating a bit better. But even with my mood lifted like that, I was still hearing my name in the stairwell, and I still fully believed those hallway cameras were tracking me. So, yes, it definitely went on for at least two weeks even when I wasn't feeling down.
Have you ever experienced a period of at least several days where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, and felt like you could accomplish anything?

No, I can't say that I have. I've never really had a time where I felt super energetic or like I didn't need to sleep. It's mostly just been the low periods... or just feeling normal, like I mentioned. But never anything like what you're describing, where I felt like I could take on the world or anything like that.
